title: A generic point in a finitely presented closed subscheme is interior
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\xi\in X$ be a generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$. If $\xi\in |i|(|Z|)$, there exists an open subscheme $N\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] with $\xi\in N$ and $|N|\subseteq |i|(|Z|)$. This is an assertion about underlying sets; it does not assert that $N\to X$ factors scheme-theoretically through $Z$. No reducedness, Noetherian or quasi-separatedness hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AAW (lemma-generic-point-in-constructible), part (1), applied to the image of a finitely presented closed immersion, as in the proof of More on Groupoids Tag 0ABB.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U\subseteq X$ containing $\xi$, and put $W=i^{-1}(U)$. By the affine description of a closed immersion, $W$ is affine. The original $i$ is locally of finite presentation, so the affine-opens finite-presentation lemma applied to $W\subseteq Z$ and $U\subseteq X$ gives a finitely presented ring map $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_Z)$. Thus $j:W\to U$ is locally of finite presentation by the definition (these two affine neighbourhoods work at every point of $W$). For every affine open $V\subseteq U$, $j^{-1}(V)=i^{-1}(V)$ is affine by the same closed-immersion description, hence quasi-compact by the affine-scheme lemma. This proves that $j$ is quasi-compact. The affine-scheme lemma also makes $U$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and the qcqs-spectral lemma therefore makes $|U|$ spectral.

source.place: Tag 0AAW (lemma-generic-point-in-constructible), affine reduction; Tag 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), (1) implies (2); Tag 054J (lemma-chevalley), checking its hypotheses

proof.text: Apply Chevalley to $j:W\to U$ and the whole source: $E=j(W)=|i|(|Z|)\cap U$ is constructible in $U$. The constructible-subset definition says these subsets form a Boolean algebra, so $F=U\setminus E$ is constructible too. The hypothesis gives $\xi\notin F$.

source.place: Tag 054J (lemma-chevalley), whole-source clause, as used in Tag 0ABB; Tag 0AAW, passage to the complement

proof.text: No point $e\in U$ other than $\xi$ specializes to $\xi$. Indeed, such a specialization also holds in $X$, and gives $C=\overline{\{\xi\}}^{X}\subseteq\overline{\{e\}}^{X}$. The closure of a singleton is irreducible: if two closed sets cover it, one contains the point and hence its whole closure. Maximality of the component $C$ forces equality of these two closures. Intersecting with $U$ gives equality of the singleton closures in $U$. Since $U$ is spectral, it is sober, and the uniqueness of the generic point of this irreducible closed subset gives $e=\xi$.

source.place: Tag 0AAW, final sentence: no different point specializes to the component generic point

proof.text: If $\xi\in\overline F^{U}$, apply the spectral proconstructible closure-specialization lemma with the singleton family whose sole member is the constructible subset $F$ of the spectral space $U$. It produces $e\in F$ with $\xi\in\overline{\{e\}}^{U}$. Step 3 forces $e=\xi$, contradicting $\xi\notin F$. Hence $\xi\notin\overline F^{U}$.

source.place: Tag 0903 (lemma-constructible-stable-specialization-closed), part (1), exactly the use in the proof of Tag 0AAW

proof.text: Set $N=U\setminus\overline F^{U}$, endowed with its open subscheme structure. It contains $\xi$. Since $F\subseteq\overline F^{U}$, its underlying set is contained in $U\setminus F=E\subseteq |i|(|Z|)$. This subset is open in $U$ and $U$ is open in $X$, so $N$ is an open subscheme of $X$ as required. Only underlying sets were used in this last inclusion.

The delivery is one commit with the item and the report, has no new nodes, and leaves statement and stmt_deps unchanged. The item is still unsplit in live and side-live and has no repair note. Step 1: the affine U gives an affine W by 01QO; the 01TQ leaf on the single pair (W,U) verifies the pointwise lfp definition for j; j is quasi-compact because preimages of affines are affine; U is qcqs and hence spectral. Step 2: Chevalley (all hypotheses checked) shows E = image ∩ U is constructible, and its complement F is constructible by the Boolean-algebra clause. Step 3: a short argument from component maximality and sobriety shows no other point of U specializes to ξ; I checked the direction of the inclusion. Step 4: the spectral closure lemma applied to the singleton family {F} plus step 3 gives ξ outside the closure of F. Step 5: N = U minus the closure of F is open, contains ξ and lies in E. Edge cases checked: empty X, the identity, a nilpotent thickening (which is why the statement is set-theoretic), and non-Noetherian X with infinitely many components. Finite presentation is used in step 2. No duplicate: searched for 0AAW, generic-point-in-constructible and the generic-point/constructible/neighbourhood statement scan. Mathlib Topology/Constructible.lean has no closure or specialization lemma for IsConstructible.
